transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. __. What brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Well, to be honest, my wife is the one who really pushed me to make the appointment. What really brought me in is that she’ll be telling me about my cousin’s appointments, or trying to organize rides for him. 

My cousin, he's been dealing with this awful sciatica lately. He can barely get in and out of a regular car, so we’ve been having to borrow my brother-in-law’s truck just to get him over to his physical therapy. And that clinic is all the way across town now because his old place shut down—something about the landlord raising the rent, I think. It's a real shame, they had good people there, especially this one guy who helped me with my shoulder a few years back... 

But anyway, what was I saying? Right, so my wife will be going over the schedule for his rides, and I’m looking right at her, but a minute later I realize I didn’t actually take in half of what she just said. I just sort of blank on it, and she gets pretty upset.
Have you had trouble with attention or forgetfulness like this since childhood?

Well, yeah, actually. I mean, even way back in grade school, well before I was 12, my parents used to hear it from my teachers all the time. They’d say I was bright, you know, but that I was always daydreaming. I’d leave my homework sitting right there in my desk, and they always had to remind me to just finish whatever we were working on in class. 

Which is funny, because my old desk at home right now looks exactly like that. I bought this beautiful oak roll-top desk at an estate sale a few years ago. The guy who owned it was a retired architect, I think, and he had all these little compartments built into it. I thought it would help me get organized, maybe sort out the bills and all the paperwork for my cousin's medical stuff. But instead, I just end up stuffing papers into all those little slots and shutting the top so I don't have to look at it. My wife hates it. She says I just bought a really expensive hiding spot for the mail. But it's solid wood, you know? They just don't make furniture like that anymore. You go to those big box stores and it's all particle board and little wooden pegs... wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, childhood. Yeah, always daydreaming, leaving stuff behind. It's been like that forever.
